commands.fixtures: two loopback HTTP fixture origins (origin and altOrigin); no production UI, dist bundle, user profile or real session is loaded

method.hostWindow: hidden BrowserWindow, webviewTag=true, sandbox=true, contextIsolation=true, nodeIntegration=false
method.guestPreferencesEnforced: will-attach-webview forces sandbox=true, contextIsolation=true, nodeIntegration=false, webSecurity=true, preload removed

mechanisms.loadURL: guest.loadURL('about:blank'); will-prevent-unload is observed but never preventDefault'ed (Electron default policy)
mechanisms.cdp: Page.enable + Page.navigate({url:'about:blank'}); Page.javascriptDialogOpening is answered inline with Page.handleJavaScriptDialog({accept:false})

method.activation: trusted CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent click on the fixture button (top frame or inside the child frame)
method.survivalProof: two executeJavaScript calls after the navigation attempt (incrementing counter + reading the pre-existing marker/draft), plus identity and Session comparison
method.commitProof: did-start-navigation(isMainFrame, about:blank) + getURL()===about:blank + marker absent in the new document
method.destroyedProof: destroyed event on the exact WebContents, isDestroyed()===true, webContents.fromId(id) empty, absence from getAllWebContents(), webview element getWebContentsId()
method.boundedTimeouts: 50s per probe process, 60s per child, 4.5s navigation settle, 3s per dialog/close wait, 2-3s per observation probe

cases.name: allow-none-loadurl
cases.purpose: Control: an unprotected guest is navigated to about:blank, then the same blank guest is closed.
cases.expectation: The blank commit succeeds, the original document is gone, and closing the blank guest destroys exactly that guest.

cases.name: allow-none-cdp
cases.purpose: Control for the CDP mechanism: Page.navigate(about:blank) commits, then the same blank guest is closed.
cases.expectation: Page.navigate reports a blank main-frame commit, the document is replaced, and closing destroys exactly that guest.

cases.name: refuse-onbeforeunload-loadurl
cases.purpose: window.onbeforeunload=()=>false with sticky activation, via loadURL(about:blank) and the default will-prevent-unload policy (never preventDefault).
cases.expectation: The navigation is cancelled, the original heap/draft/identity/session survive, and the guest still executes JS after the attempt.

cases.name: refuse-onbeforeunload-cdp
cases.purpose: window.onbeforeunload=()=>false with sticky activation, via CDP Page.navigate(about:blank) and an explicit deny of the beforeunload dialog.
cases.expectation: The navigation is cancelled (dialog denied), the original heap/draft/identity/session survive, and the guest still executes JS.

cases.name: refuse-listener-loadurl
cases.purpose: addEventListener(beforeunload) + preventDefault, via loadURL(about:blank) and the default policy.
cases.expectation: The navigation is cancelled and the original document survives if the modern listener form is honoured.

cases.name: refuse-listener-cdp
cases.purpose: addEventListener(beforeunload) + preventDefault, via CDP Page.navigate(about:blank) with an explicit deny.
cases.expectation: The navigation is cancelled and the original document survives if the modern listener form is honoured.

cases.name: refuse-late-loadurl
cases.purpose: Race: the protection is installed 250ms AFTER the loadURL(about:blank) starts.
cases.expectation: Exploratory: the navigation decision is expected to already be in flight, so the late handler is not expected to cancel it.

cases.name: refuse-late-cdp
cases.purpose: Race: the protection is installed 250ms AFTER the CDP Page.navigate(about:blank) starts.
cases.expectation: Exploratory: same race as the loadURL variant, through the CDP navigation path.

cases.name: refuse-iframe-same-loadurl
cases.purpose: A same-origin child frame with its own beforeunload handler, frame itself activated, top frame navigated by loadURL.
cases.expectation: Exploratory: measures whether a child-frame refusal can cancel the top-level navigation.

cases.name: refuse-iframe-same-cdp
cases.purpose: Same-origin child frame with beforeunload, frame activated, top frame navigated by CDP Page.navigate.
cases.expectation: Exploratory: measures whether a child-frame refusal can cancel the top-level navigation over CDP.

cases.name: refuse-iframe-cross-loadurl
cases.purpose: A cross-origin (second loopback origin) child frame with beforeunload, frame activated, top frame navigated by loadURL.
cases.expectation: Exploratory: measures whether a cross-origin child-frame refusal can cancel the top-level navigation.

cases.name: refuse-iframe-cross-cdp
cases.purpose: Cross-origin child frame with beforeunload, frame activated, top frame navigated by CDP Page.navigate.
cases.expectation: Exploratory: measures whether a cross-origin child-frame refusal can cancel the top-level navigation over CDP.

cases.name: refuse-noactivation-loadurl
cases.purpose: Control: onbeforeunload exists but the guest has no sticky activation, so no refusal dialog should be available.
cases.expectation: Without activation the navigation commits; a refusal observed here would be invalid evidence for a cancellable path.

cases.name: refuse-noactivation-cdp
cases.purpose: Control for CDP: onbeforeunload exists but the guest has no sticky activation.
cases.expectation: Without activation the CDP navigation commits and no beforeunload dialog is expected.

cases.name: race-demand-during-nav
cases.purpose: Race: a close demand (guest.close({waitForBeforeUnload:true})) arrives 30ms after the protected navigation starts.
cases.expectation: Exploratory only; records which of navigation / unload policy / close demand wins. No production conclusion is asserted.

conclusion.recommendation: The tested navigation path is cancellable in this runtime: a refusing guest keeps its heap, draft, identity and Session, and a committing blank guest can be closed separately. This is still only fixture evidence; production still needs activation/demand protocol design and its own acceptance.
statements: loadURL('about:blank') committed for an unprotected guest: true.
The blank commit replaced the original document: true.
Closing the guest after the blank commit destroyed exactly that guest: true.
will-prevent-unload fired on a refused loadURL navigation: true.
loadURL(about:blank) navigation was cancelled by onbeforeunload refusal: true.
The refused loadURL navigation kept the original JS heap: true.
The refused loadURL navigation kept the DOM draft: true.
The refused loadURL navigation kept guest identity and native Session: true.
The guest still executed JS twice after the refused loadURL navigation: true.
CDP Page.navigate(about:blank) navigation was cancelled by an explicitly denied beforeunload dialog: true.
A CDP beforeunload dialog opened on that navigation: true.
The denied CDP navigation kept the original JS heap: true.
addEventListener(beforeunload) cancelled the navigation (loadURL / CDP): true / true.
Without sticky activation the navigation committed: true.
A protection installed after the navigation started still cancelled it (loadURL / CDP): false / false.
A same-origin child-frame refusal cancelled the top navigation (loadURL / CDP): true / true.
A cross-origin child-frame refusal cancelled the top navigation (loadURL / CDP): true / true.

rawEvidence.note: Raw child reports contain only fixture URLs, loopback ports and relative profile paths; no credentials, tokens or environment dumps are written.

limitations: Three rounds per case; timings are observations, not latency percentiles.
Hidden unfocused fixture window and synthetic (CDP Input) activation; visible/focused-window behaviour and real hardware input were not tested.
about:blank is a special case (no network); navigation to real URLs, redirects, POST bodies and cross-origin top-level targets were not tested.
Fixtures are synthetic loopback pages with no service workers, no cookies, no authentication and no real account or network.
The child-frame cases measure whether a frame refusal cancels the top-level navigation; they are exploratory and do not assert production correctness.
The demand race case is exploratory: it records event ordering only and asserts no production conclusion.
beforeunload refusal semantics can differ for navigations initiated by the user vs. the embedder; only embedder-initiated navigation (loadURL / CDP Page.navigate) was tested.
A draft value was installed by script in most cases and typed via trusted input only for top-activation cases; it proves document survival, not editor integration.
Child reports are bounded (event cap, truncated console text); full page internals beyond the recorded probes were not inspected.
